doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: Chris's haunts and friends; George Lewis at the house
summary: Edna recalls Chris drinking wine at a speakeasy and names friends. George Lewis was at the house daily, a slender brown-skinned man.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. Can you remember any stories or anecdotes or anything about Chris, you know, like any incidents or anything at all that would just be of some interest to, you know, colorful or something to remember? Like what? Like where he used to go? Yeah, like where he used to go or?

He used to go to Rudy Dooley's and drink wine all the time. Where's that? Used to call him Rudy Dooley. There's a man by the name of Rudy Dooley. What? He used to have a speakeasy and go in there and drink wine. Where was that? That was on St. Anne Street. St. Anne's General. Oh, my God.
Who were some of his friends that you come up with?

I was so long, I'm dead so long. I'm back here now. We came from that place. See, I moved back here with me. And he told I no father about that. I was mine. But I know. I know George Burns, but he waited on the nightfall. I don't know where he lived. George Burns. I can't think. I know every one of them, but they all know. About stuff
Did he see George Lewis very often or was it just to meet you?
Well, every day George Lewis used to be at our house. He used to stay there almost. Really? Sure. Every day.
What was George like? What sort of a fashion?

He was kind of slender, brown-skinned fella with red lips and he would be smiling nice. And then he had a wife and a gang of children on this side of the river and he was on the other side of the river.
Right. He didn't move on the other side of the river until, what, 1950s?
Oh no, long time after Chris died. Right. Long time. But he went for himself after Chris died. He got big there and grew bigger.
